name: Gravity: Analog Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor, corrosion resistant (bare-PCB probe with a PH2.0-3P plug)
//: Catalog record written by /spark:research on 2026-09-29 while researching a garden-bed soil probe for the irrigation project: the part read, evaluated and NOT chosen (see //why_not). A draft — filled only from what was actually read, everything else null. WHAT IT IS TRUE OF: DFRobot SKU SEN0193 as drawn in the vendor's schematic 'Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor, Revision V1.0, 2015/8/27, drawn Bernie-SH', the only schematic the vendor publishes. verified: true = the vendor's own text at the cited URL; read off an image or a drawing, inferred or computed = false with why_it_matters.
//why_not: Its electronics are an exposed PCB that must stay above the soil line, and the need was a garden bed; DFRobot's own SEN0308 page names 'long-term outdoor gardening' and gives that one the IP65 head — for a pot indoors this is the pick, at a quarter of the price.
//chosen_instead: sen0308-soil-moisture, the IP65 sibling, in the irrigation project's parts/; it names this record under alternatives.
also_known_as: Gravity: Analog Capacitive Corrosion Resistant Soil Moisture Sensor for Arduino / Raspberry Pi
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor SKU SEN0193
//sources: Every URL below was fetched during research; `parts.py --sources` re-fetches them and `parts.py --fetch` keeps the PDF and the photo beside this record.

needs.note: Yellow wire of the supplied Gravity analog cable (the wiki's calibration page: red to VCC, black to GND, yellow to Signal). A DC level that falls as the soil gets wetter: 'There is an inverse ratio between the sensor output value and soil moisture.'

power.note: Red wire. The vendor allows 3.3 ~ 5.5 V. Put on the 3.3 V rail here for the same reason as the SEN0308 record; on this part the output is bounded by its own 3.0 V regulator IF the drawing reading in facts.timer_supply_rail holds, so 5 V would be safe too. A draft's decision, not the vendor's.

//pin_order: J1 'CON/SIP3' on the V1.0 schematic: 1 GND, 2 VCC, 3 Signal — read off the drawing, so verified: false (facts.connector_pin_order). It is the order of the PH2.0-3P socket on the probe; the supplied Gravity analog cable mates it pin for pin, so the board's socket copies this order.
//footprint: The wiki's 'Interface PH2.0-3P' is a JST PH 2.0 mm 3-pin socket, so the board needs the mating 3-pin PH socket for the supplied cable. Whether footprinter has a 3-pin PH string (jst_ph_3?) was not checked, so this stays null until someone builds with it.
//on_board: It stands in the soil at the end of the supplied analog sensor cable; the board carries only the mating socket.

body_mm.source: https://www.dfrobot.com/product-1385.html — 'Dimensions: 98mm * 23mm (3.86in x 0.905in)'; the wiki table gives 3.86 x 0.905 inches (L x W)
body_mm.note: The whole PCB, blade plus the electronics end. Off-board, so nothing is placed around it.

supply_range_v.note: 'Operating Voltage 3.3 ~ 5.5 VDC' in the wiki table and on the product page.

output_range_v.why_it_matters: It has to fit under a 3.3 V ADC's ceiling. The vendor disagrees with itself: the wiki table says 'Output Voltage 0 ~ 3.0VDC', the product page says '1.2 ~ 2.5V'. A poster on the vendor's forum (2023) quotes 637 counts in air and 1 in water on a 10-bit ADC and '1.14 V' in soil at an input of 4.6 V — about 3.1 V in air if the reference was 5 V — so the wiki's 3.0 V ceiling is the figure to design against, not the product page's 2.5 V.

operating_current_ma.note: 'Operating Current 5mA' in the wiki table; the product page does not state it.

interface.note: A JST PH 2.0 mm 3-pin socket, DFRobot's Gravity analog interface. The product page's shipping list: 'Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor x1, Analog Sensor Cable x1'.

timer_ic.note: IC2, SOP-8, named in the schematic's own text. The blade is driven by this astable timer; the output is the peak-detected level behind D1 (1N4148WS) with R1 1 M and C3 1 uF to ground.

regulator.note: IC1, SOT-23, described in the schematic's own text as a '3.0V voltage regulator IC', fed from VCC with 100 nF + 4.7 uF on each side.

timer_supply_rail.value: 3.0 V (IC2 pin 8 on the regulator's 3.0V net)
timer_supply_rail.why_it_matters: If the timer runs from the 3.0 V rail, its square wave and so the peak-detected output cannot exceed 3.0 V whatever VCC is — which is what would make this part safe for a 3.3 V ADC even on a 5 V supply. Read off the drawing, not the vendor's text: confirm on the drawing, or on the bench by feeding 5 V and checking that the dry-air output stays below 3.0 V.

connector_pin_order.why_it_matters: It is the order the board's PH socket must copy, and it was read off the drawing. Swapped VCC and GND reverses the probe; confirm against the plug on the delivered part before a board is ordered.

detector_time_constant_s.why_it_matters: R1 1 M across C3 1 uF, computed from two values read off the drawing: the output settles over seconds, so a power-gated probe needs several seconds before its first trusted sample.

reading_falls_as_soil_wets.note: 'There is an inverse ratio between the sensor output value and soil moisture.' The vendor's calibration: the reading in air is the 0 % reference, the reading in water (not past the red line) the 100 % reference.

electronics_must_stay_dry.why_it_matters: The calibration page says to insert the probe into water 'not past the red line': the electronics end is a bare PCB. In a garden bed that line is the difference between a sensor and a corroded one, which is why the IP65 sibling was chosen for that need.

hardware_revision.why_it_matters: The vendor's forum carries a 2023 thread titled 'Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor V.2' (https://www.dfrobot.com/forum/topic/321676) that discusses readings only and names no hardware change, and neither wiki nor product page mentions a revision. If a later revision changed the regulator or the connector, the schematic-derived facts here are about the wrong board; read the silkscreen on the delivered part.

host_requirements: Keep the electronics end above the soil and out of the rain: the PCB is bare, the vendor's own calibration says 'not past the red line', and nothing on it is rated for ingress.

The output tops out at 3.0 V by the wiki's own table (1.2-2.5 V by the product page), so a 3.3 V ADC reads it from either rail — but calibrate air and water per probe at the supply the board gives it; the vendor's counts come from a 5 V UNO.
On an ESP32 with Wi-Fi on, read it on an ADC1 pin, and average several samples.

sourcing.note: USD 5.90 direct; ships from China. No local (Czech) listing was fetched for this part.
